traces.text: The question wants me to get information on all department's subjects (excluding the Math department) that grant a degree which were offered in the 2022 academic year. They want the school name, department, the average total units of each subject, as well as the range and variance of the total units for each subject. In addition to this unit information, I am asked for enrollment information for each department in the school of engineering save for management that both grants degrees and hasa total student enrollment over 50. For that, they want the department, the total enrollment, and the most popular course measured by enrollment along with it's enrollment count. I am to lable each record in the result as 'UnitStats' or 'EnrollmentStats' with the ordered columns of school name, department name, average total units, total units range, total units variance, total enrollment, most popular course, course enrollment, and reason. Starting with the unit information, I get the school and department information from teh SIS_COURSE_DESCRIPTION table and get the total units from COURSE_CATALOG_SUBJECT_OFFERED -- I join them via COURSE and SUBJECT_CODE respectively. Then I filter on the catalog academic year of 2022, and then for the course descrption, focus on degree_granting = 'Y' and exclude the 'Mathematics' department_name as well as the respective code for math (18). From there I can aggregate by department from that CTE by selecting SCHOOL_NAME, DEPARTMENT_NAME, and DEPARTMENT, then I can average the total units, subtract the min from the max for the range, and use the built in variance function for the variance of total_units across subjects within the department, and then I just GROUP BY the non-aggregated fields. For the second question on enrollment, I cna use the SIS_DEPARTMENT and TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED tables and join on them via DEPARTMENT_CODE and OFFER_DEPT_CODE respectively. From the dept table I can get the department name and the code, from the subject table I can get the number of enrolled students NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS. I will sum it and alias that as total_enrollment and group by the department columns. I will filter on the department school_name to be 'Engineering' have degree granting at 'Y' and exclude the management dept of code 15. I will use a HAVING clause to ensure total_enrollment is above 50. From this CTE I can get the department information and total enrollment and then concatenate that to the most popular course and it's enrollment by JOINing on TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED using the department code we selected and filtering the subject table with a nested SELECT MAX num enrolled students in the WHERE clause. Now I can stack the results by unioning them and aligning common columns. I can default 'Engineering' as the school name for the second result set.
